solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Idiot copper's put into cell

indicators.note: something put into another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A foolish policeman gets locked up in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'cell' paint a police scene, but the copper is the metal and the cell is biological: an ascus is the spore sac of certain fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany an ascus is a sac-shaped cell in which fungal spores form.

clue.text: Woman in temple and saint set up sums for certain widows

indicators.note: in a down clue, something set up is raised so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Anna the prophetess greeted the infant Jesus in the Temple (Luke 2)
standard abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A woman at a temple and a saint arrange payments for widows.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the saint is turned round; the biblical Anna stays as she is. Annat is a Scots law term.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law annats were the half-year's stipend paid to the widow or family of a deceased minister.

clue.text: Fish about to be brought into stations

indicators.note: brought into means placed inside something else, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: stations or seats are places where people are positioned
ca. is circa, about

explanation.surface: Fish are carried around and delivered to fishing stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea cat is a name for several fish, such as the wolffish and some catfish.

clue.text: Chalet in July/August period in biblical location

indicators.note: the period sits in the place, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Cana in Galilee, scene of the wedding where water became wine
Ab (Av) is the Jewish month falling in July and August

explanation.surface: A holiday chalet rented for midsummer somewhere in the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'July/August period' sounds like a holiday booking, but it is the Hebrew calendar month Ab.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabana is a small hut or cabin, especially a beach shelter, like a simple chalet.

clue.text: Vengeance shown by sailors in a complete reversal

blocks.note: utu is a Maori word for revenge or retribution, found in Chambers
the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors take revenge by turning the ship right round.
explanation.walkthrough: UTU is a New Zealand word for vengeance; 'shown by' just places the sailors next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn is a turn through 180 degrees, hence any total about-face in policy or direction.

clue.text: Alien can't learn English? Special training needed

indicators.note: alien means strange or foreign, so the following letters are put into a strange new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A foreigner unable to pick up the language needs extra tuition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternance training is a scheme that alternates periods of classroom study with periods of work experience.

clue.text: First-class chums around at Oxford?

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: pals are friends
a student in residence at a university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Friends hanging about an Oxford college, as smart as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford is British usage for being in residence at the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, excellent one, so the phrase is informal for top-quality.

clue.text: Sing of a land divorced from reality?

definitions.text: of a land divorced from reality
definitions.note: adjectival: the la-la of la-la land

blocks.note: first meaning: to sing wordless syllables, crooning tra-la

blocks.clueFragment: of a land divorced from reality
blocks.note: second meaning: describing ... land, a dreamy fantasy world

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a song about a dreamland; the answer is both a verb for vocalising and the first word of the phrase for a fantasy place.
explanation.definitionFit: La-la land is an idiom for a state of being out of touch with the real world, and to la-la is to sing nonsense syllables.

clue.text: Excited, sitting by the fire?

blocks.note: sitting at a place means being by it
an ingle is a fireplace or hearth fire

explanation.surface: Someone warm and thrilled while seated beside the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a cosy picture: to be 'at ingle' is to be at the fireside, an inglenook being a chimney corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Atingle means tingling all over, a state of thrilled anticipation.

clue.text: Hope abandoned with nothing gained, end of story? Nonsense!

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept
abandoned suggests wild and unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
zero, nought
the last letter of the word story

explanation.surface: Abandoning hope and getting nowhere: the end of the story? Rubbish!
explanation.definitionFit: Phooey is an exclamation of scornful disbelief, the same as saying rubbish.

clue.text: Presumably bust, in need of alms somehow — somehow secure earlier?

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the long word is broken up and its letters rearranged
a word in need of something lacks it, so those letters are taken away
in some way or other: the removed letters are scattered rather than in a run
in some way or other: what remains is put in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, its letters removed in any order

explanation.surface: Someone presumably broke, begging, still manages to get hold of something in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters of alms appear scattered through the long word, not as a run; once they go, the six letters left over are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To prebuy is to purchase ahead of time, to obtain something before it is needed.

clue.text: Smart shelter redesigned, lined with a tough material

indicators.note: a building redesigned has its parts rearranged, so these letters are reordered
something lined with a thing has it inside, so a piece goes within

blocks.note: neat means tidy, smart
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smart shelter is rebuilt and lined with something hard-wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' here is the old word for cattle as well as meaning smart, which is how the leather gets its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat's leather is leather made from the hide of an ox or cow, a durable material.

clue.text: Greek in one story one set of books covered

indicators.note: something covered is wrapped by something else, so these pieces sit inside the story

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a tale is a story
Roman numeral one
the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A Greek appears in a story that covers a set of books.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'one' and the books go inside the tale; the first 'one' stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italiote was a Greek inhabitant of the ancient colonies in southern Italy.

clue.text: Something unimportant making one terribly paranoid — stop getting involved

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters of the word are badly jumbled
something involved is wrapped up inside, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
ho is an old call to halt, as in whoa

explanation.surface: A trivial matter makes someone wildly suspicious, so they stop meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making one' only links definition to wordplay: the trivial thing makes one paranoid.
explanation.definitionFit: In theology an adiaphoron is a matter of indifference, neither commanded nor forbidden, so not important.

clue.text: Small creatures in major road blocking vehicle

indicators.note: a road blocking the way stands either side, so it wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: the A1, Britain's longest numbered road, written A-one
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Tiny animals on a main road are getting in a car's way.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the great road from London to Edinburgh; the I stands for its numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Acari are mites and ticks, tiny arachnids.

clue.text: Beginner is jovial when knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: boon means jolly and convivial, as in a boon companion

explanation.surface: A cheerful novice is knocked flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Noob is gaming and internet slang for a newcomer or novice.

clue.text: Old money for one who's helped make 11?

blocks.note: first meaning: a pre-decimal British sixpence coin
second meaning: a worker who treats hides, the answer to 11 being a kind of leather

explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was slang for the old sixpenny piece; the cross-reference points to NEAT'S LEATHER, which a tanner produces.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a sixpence coin and also names a craftsman who converts hides into leather.

clue.text: Artless young chap at home, dope of the upper-classes

blocks.note: someone at home is in
gen and dope are both slang for information
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U usage

explanation.surface: A naive young man at home, an upper-class idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' wants to be a fool, which fits the naive young chap, but it is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénu is a naive, innocent young man, the male form of ingénue.

clue.text: Botanical part's found in grit by lake

definitions.note: possessive, standing for the adjective: of a stamen

blocks.note: grit is endurance
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A plant part turns up in the gravel beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grit' looks like sand by the lake but means staying power.
explanation.definitionFit: Staminal is the adjective for a stamen, the pollen-bearing organ of a flower.

clue.text: Black male with vigour and style in charge

blocks.note: abbreviation for male
élan is flair and energy
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A dark man with energy and flair takes command.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanic means having dark pigmentation from melanin.

clue.text: Man is repeatedly confused with apes

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters are put in muddled order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word is used twice

explanation.surface: Humans are often mistaken for apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' doubles the little word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Simians are monkeys and apes, the primate group.

clue.text: Grass in school overlooking river

indicators.note: to overlook something is to miss it out, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a grammar school
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Grass growing at a school that looks down on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A British grammar school is a selective state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Gramma is a type of pasture grass of the American prairies.

clue.text: Loud insect makes splash

blocks.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud
a louse is a small insect

explanation.surface: A noisy bug makes a big splash.
explanation.definitionFit: Flouse is a dialect verb meaning to splash or dash water about.

clue.text: Like some languages in journal lacking particular letters?

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for journal
aphesis is the loss of an unstressed initial vowel, as in squire from esquire

explanation.surface: Certain languages, in a magazine that leaves out some letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking particular letters' reads as a typo description, but it defines a linguistic term.
explanation.definitionFit: Japhetic was an old label for the Indo-European languages, supposedly descended from Noah's son Japheth.

clue.text: Old Muslim not wanting Sikh symbol gets to prohibit … this?

definitions.text: Old Muslim not wanting Sikh symbol gets to prohibit … this?

indicators.note: not wanting something means going without it, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: Turk was an old name for any Muslim
the five Ks are the symbols of Sikh faith
to ban is to forbid

explanation.surface: Would a Turk wish to ban the Sikh headdress?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a whole: the thing an old Muslim without a K wants to prohibit is itself a Sikh symbol, though it is not one of the five Ks.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a long cloth wound round the head, worn by Sikh men as a sign of faith.

clue.text: Church getting to mark place of sacrifice?

blocks.note: Church of England
to note is to mark or observe

explanation.surface: A church is set to commemorate a site of sacrifice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenote is a natural limestone sinkhole in Yucatán into which the Maya threw sacrificial offerings.

clue.text: Arrive en masse fishing with banks to be avoided

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its two edges, and avoiding them means leaving those off

blocks.note: trolling is fishing by trailing a line behind a boat

explanation.surface: Anglers arrive in crowds to fish away from the riverbanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suits the fishing picture, but it means the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll in is to arrive in large numbers or quantities.

clue.text: Helmet made of gold coated with particular pigment

indicators.note: something coated is wrapped in an outer layer, which goes around it

blocks.note: heme (haem) is the iron-containing pigment in haemoglobin
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A golden helmet painted in a special colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A heaume is a large medieval helmet enclosing the whole head.

clue.text: Lizard eaten by stag — amazing!

indicators.note: something eaten by other words is swallowed inside them, so the answer lies within

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A lizard gets eaten by a deer: astonishing!
explanation.walkthrough: Deer are herbivores, which is why the surface exclaims.
explanation.definitionFit: An agama is an Old World lizard of the family Agamidae.

clue.text: A rescuer of animals has tail cut off wild beast

indicators.note: cutting off a tail removes the end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
Noah saved the animals in the Ark

explanation.surface: An animal rescuer has the tail of a wild creature cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: The anoa is a small wild buffalo of Sulawesi.

clue.text: Six no trumps in a card game

blocks.note: Roman numeral six
the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: A bid of six no trumps in a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Six no trumps sounds like a bridge bid, but six is a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Vint is a Russian card game similar to whist and bridge.

clue.text: A never-ending dull task that's done — no longer with a smile

indicators.note: something never-ending has no end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a grind is tedious work

explanation.surface: Once an endless chore is finished, you are left grinning.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle phrase tells the story: the chore is done and no longer a grind, so its last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrin is an adverb meaning grinning, in the manner of someone smiling broadly.

clue.text: New menu that is about to be offered — food may be presented thus

indicators.note: a new version of something has its form changed, so the letters are put in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
i.e. is id est, that is
re means concerning

explanation.surface: A new restaurant menu is about to be served up.
explanation.definitionFit: À la meunière describes fish dusted with flour and fried in butter, a style of serving it.

clue.text: Liar currently succeeding with article — something hazy about that

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the haze wraps around the other pieces

blocks.note: mist is a haze
in form means performing well at present
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dishonest person is doing well writing an article that is vague on the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A misinformant gives false information, which is what a liar does.

clue.text: Beer firm admitting contaminant finally? Fury is result

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word before it
admitting means letting in, so a piece goes inside the firm

blocks.note: ale is beer
Co. is the abbreviation for company
the final letter of the word contaminant

explanation.surface: A brewery lets in something toxic, and rage follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fury' looks like the anger that results, but it is one of the three Furies of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecto is one of the three Erinyes, the Furies of Greek mythology.

clue.text: Special house staff, time-wasting group

indicators.note: wasting time here means losing the time symbol, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to man is to staff
a set is a group
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A special house whose staff are an idle crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is a minister's residence, a house set aside for the clergy.
